sn47.1:1.1: The Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta lacks a detailed set of meditation practices such as those found in the great meditation compilations the Satipaṭṭhānasutta ([mn10](),[dn22]()) and the Kāyagatāsatisutta ([]()).
sn47.1:1.2: Ambapālī was a courtesan who offered this land to the Saṅgha. She later went forth as a *bhikkhunī*; her verses are at [thig13.1](). This is an excerpt from the narrative at [dn16:2.11.5]().
sn47.1:2.1: See [sn47.18]() for notes on _ekāyana_. | A _ñāya_ is a “system”, method, or way of practice that proceeds in line with cause and effect. It refers to the pattern of the Buddha’s teaching, especially dependent origination ([sn12.41:12.1](), [an10.92:6.1](); see too [an4.35:3.5]()).
